excerpt: Assess Dubai South property investment opportunities and risks through current infrastructure, project delivery, rental evidence and competing supply.
introduction:
Dubai South combines residential development with aviation and logistics activity, but a large infrastructure plan does not guarantee the performance of an individual apartment. Compare the exact project, current services, purchase cost, tenant demand and future competition before treating the area as an investment.

This guide separates official infrastructure announcements from assumptions about property returns. The worked numbers show how to compare the investment costs for two apartments.
takeaways: Distinguish announced airport expansion and long-term plans from facilities operating today.
Check the specific unit's registration, construction status, access, building costs and comparable leases.
Test vacancy, service charges, project delays and resale risk instead of assuming infrastructure guarantees gains.

sections.heading: What is the long-term infrastructure context?
sections.body:
Dubai's [Government Media Office announced in April 2024](https://mediaoffice.ae/en/news/2024/april/28-04/al-maktoum-international-airport) approval of designs for a new Al Maktoum International Airport passenger terminal, with an announced AED 128 billion cost and long-term capacity plans. These are plans for aviation infrastructure, not evidence of a return on a specific home.

In a [September 2026 media briefing](https://cd1.mediaoffice.ae/en/news/2026/september/11-09/dubai-airports-ceo-outlines-dxb-growth-and-future-of-dubai-aviation), Dubai Airports' chief executive said the first major phase was on track for the early 2030s. That is a stated outlook at the time, not an already completed facility or a guarantee that a particular property will appreciate.

Check the latest official progress and the exact route from the building. The [Dubai area comparison](/journal/jvc-vs-arjan-apartment-investment-comparison) provides a method for comparing a different location on unit-level evidence.

sections.heading: What is available to a resident today?
sections.body:
Dubai South's [Residential District update](https://www.dubaisouth.ae/en/newsroom/dubai-south-sells-out-south-living-project-confirms-huge-demand-for-spacious-units-in-the-area) describes existing amenities and residential development. As a developer source, it is useful for identifying facilities to verify, but project-specific availability and operating hours may change.

Visit the exact location and check roads, parking, shops, school access and public transport relevant to the intended tenant. Ask schools about admission and transport rather than assuming a place. Test travel at the time it would be used; a planned connection or headline journey time is not the same as current service from the building.

Inspect the apartment and common areas, or for off-plan request the contracted specification and dated construction evidence. A district description cannot establish the quality of one unit.

sections.heading: Test rent and owner costs
sections.body:
Use recent signed leases for comparable apartments, adjusting for size, condition, furnishing, parking and included services. Subtract vacancy and owner-paid service charges, management, repairs and insurance. Divide net operating income by full acquisition cost. The [Dubai net yield guide](/journal/how-to-calculate-net-rental-yield-in-dubai) explains the calculation.

For a sample property costing AED 1,000,000 in total, suppose one scenario has AED 70,000 rent and AED 20,000 in vacancy and owner costs, leaving AED 50,000 or 5%. A weaker scenario assumes AED 60,000 rent and AED 25,000 in vacancy and costs, leaving AED 35,000 or 3.5%. These example inputs show how the purchase cost and annual income fit into the calculation.

The chart compares the resulting annual income before finance, tax and sale costs. Neither scenario is a prediction or a guarantee.

sections.heading: Check project delivery and supply
sections.body:
For off-plan, verify the project and developer through DLD's [project status enquiry](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/real-estate-project-status-landing/real-estate-project-status/). Check the contract, payment recipient, initial registration, handover provisions and current progress. Keep sufficient cash for instalments even if the project or your plans are delayed.

Look at scheduled nearby handovers and the number and type of units that could compete for similar tenants. Future supply is a schedule, not proof that all units will be completed or vacant at the same time. Ask for evidence and update it as the project progresses.

A payment plan can change cash timing, but it does not by itself make the underlying purchase price attractive. Compare ready and off-plan alternatives on total cost and risk.

sections.heading: Assess the exit and holding period
sections.body:
Seek completed sales of genuinely similar properties where available and separate them from asking prices. Consider selling charges, any remaining loan and the time needed to find a buyer. An infrastructure announcement may influence expectations, but the timing and effect on a particular unit are uncertain.

Test a longer holding period, a lower rent and a sale price below the purchase price. Keep a reserve for repairs and periods without a tenant. If the investment works only when a projected airport milestone produces immediate growth, the plan is exposed to assumptions outside your control.

Verify the ownership right for the buyer, title or initial registration, building obligations and current official charges for the unit.

sections.heading: Check the building's ongoing obligations
sections.body:
Ask for the current service-charge statement or, for a new project, the estimate and basis of calculation. Confirm whether the figure is approved, which shared services it covers and when the final amount will be known. Include utility or cooling charges that the owner may have to pay while the unit is empty.

Review the developer's and building management's contact details, maintenance arrangements and any remaining payment obligations. A planned amenity may be valuable to a future tenant, but check whether it is part of the signed specification and whether it is operating. Keep those distinctions in the comparison.

sections.heading: Explore specific Dubai South projects
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Dubai South project collection](/projects?emirate=Dubai&area=dubai-south) and ask which units are currently available. [Contact Aliyas](/contact) with your budget, intended tenant and holding period to request the exact plan, price, payment schedule and documents.

Compare those details with current lease and construction evidence before committing. Use the same criteria to assess the apartment's potential income, annual costs and intended holding period.
